programmes.customer_access: Not described on the apply or cohort pages.
programmes.network_quality: Very high. antler.co/about: offices in 27 cities; 'PitchBook ranked Antler as the most active VC globally, Dealroom recognized the firm as the most active investor in AI startups'.
programmes.brand_value: High globally, high density in the Nordics.
programmes.application_effort: ~1 hour for the short form; add 1-2 hours if submitting the pitch form, which takes an optional deck upload (10MB max). No video required. No references required.
programmes.notes: Strongest single row in the lane and it survived verification intact: rolling, no entity, founder-first, form loads and takes input today. Bangalore is also a selectable Antler city, so a Nordic visa problem does not end the application. Two corrections to carry forward: (a) every funding and perks figure attributed to Antler in phase 1 is from secondary press and appears NOWHERE on antler.co, so do not quote them in an application or to the founder; (b) the apply page has no visa wording at all.

programmes.name: Slush 100 Startup Competition
programmes.page_evidence: The programme page invites applications now and the window is live: the timeline reads 'Aug 12 – Applications open', 'Sep 7 – Applications close', 'Sep 11 – Top 100 selected', 'Oct 1 – Top 20 semifinalists', 'Nov 18 – Semifinal; Top 3 finalists', 'Nov 19 – Final; winner announced'. Today is 2026-08-14, inside that window, and slush.org/audience/startups/startups lists Slush 100 as 'Applications open'. Sign up'. I could not see the form fields.

programmes.cash: 'The winner of the Slush 100 competition gets €500,000 with 0% equity from Slush', plus a speaking slot at Slush 2027. Secondary reporting separately describes General Catalyst and Cherry Ventures backing the winner with €1,000,000 in equity funding — that is NOT on the Slush page I read and should not be quoted as fact.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity-free for the Slush prize: '0% equity', 'no strings attached, no reporting burden, no ties.'

programmes.brand_value: Very high, and the cash is equity-free.

Slush advises 'make sure your company profile is up-to-date and that you've attached a pitch deck.' No video requirement found. A deck is effectively required.

The eligibility line is unambiguous: 'Any startup that has been incorporated during or after 2023 and has raised less than €10,000,000 in equity fundraising can apply.' That is an incorporation criterion on the programme's own page, so entity_required_to_apply is true. I could NOT test whether the form actually rejects a blank incorporation field because the account gate stopped me. Given the €500K equity-free prize this is worth 15 minutes: create a free Slush Platform account and look at the company-profile form before writing anything off. Also note the phase-1 apply URL (platform.slush.org/public/slush26/activities/launch?side_event_id=...) is dead — HTTP 404.

programmes.name: StartupLab Accelerator (edition #19)

File this one — a deck is the only artefact needed.

programmes.network_quality: Government gateway rather than a network.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a signal, high as a key: it is the precondition that unlocks Innofounder for a non-EU founder.
programmes.application_effort: Two-step. Step 1: business plan to the expert panel (est. 15-25 hours). Step 2: SIRI residence and work permit application. CORRECTION to phase 1: the SIRI processing fee is 'DKK 3,060,-', not DKK 1,900. Self-support documentation of DKK 153,240-356,904 (2025 levels, by family composition) is also required.
programmes.notes: Non-EU nationality is a REQUIREMENT here, not a barrier — the page says outright 'This program is not for EU citizens due to the free mobility within the EU.' The founder qualifies where an EU citizen would not. Quota: 'a maximum of 75 foreign nationals can be granted a permit based on the scheme per year.' This is the gate that must clear before Innofounder or Beyond Beta become reachable, and at 2-4 months processing plus a 12-month Innofounder cycle, that is a 2027 plan, not a 2026 one.

programmes.name: Innofounder — Round 2 2026
programmes.page_evidence: VERIFIED: 'E-grant open for submission of application: from July 28, 2026 to August 25, 2026, at 12:00 PM'. The window is live today.
programmes.cohort_dates: 'The Innofounder course lasts 12 months.'
programmes.cash: Three tiers by team size — Small (1 founder), Medium (2 founders), Large (3 founders). The official page does not itemise the amounts. The DKK 27,500/month plus DKK 100,000 development grant figure is secondary and unverified on innovationsfonden.dk.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly welcomes solo: 'You can apply both as an individual and as an entrepreneurial team of up to 3 founders.' The Small tier exists specifically for one founder.
programmes.location_requirement: Denmark. 'You must have established a company with a Danish CVR number when the Innofounder process starts' — at programme start, not at submission.
programmes.customer_access: Danish ecosystem; not detailed.
programmes.network_quality: Danish ecosystem, state-backed.
programmes.application_effort: e-grant.dk submission, est. 8-15 hours. Requires proof of completed higher education: 'You can apply for Innofounder if you have completed a higher education before the start of the course.'
programmes.hard_blocker: Residence permit not held. The page requires that non-EU/EEA applicants have 'a Start-up Denmark visa, or have obtained your education from a Danish educational institution or have worked for at least 1 year in a company / public institution in Denmark.' The founder is an Indian national in Bangalore with a German (TUM) degree and no Danish work history, and holds no Start-up Denmark visa. This is a genuine eligibility wall at application time, not a paperwork gap.
programmes.notes: The blocker is sequential rather than absolute — Startup Denmark approval first (2-4 months), Innofounder second — but it cannot be cleared in the 11 days remaining on this round. A real target for round 1 2027 IF the Danish route is pursued at all. The TUM degree satisfies the higher-education criterion; it is the permit line alone that stops this.

programmes.name: Estonian Startup Visa
programmes.page_evidence: The Startup Estonia page invites applications with no deadline and no closure notice, and serves the Dealum apply link directly. The Dealum form is a JavaScript single-page app that returns an empty body to a plain fetch, so I could not enumerate its fields — but the referring page invites applications now.
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling. Startup Committee decision typically within 10 working days, then embassy issuance. Initially 12 months, extendable by six months, then convertible to a temporary residence permit for up to five years.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Holders can use e-Residency for remote company management.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement published.
programmes.location_requirement: Estonia. The startup must be 'a technology-based, innovative, and scalable business that has an MVP and the first traction', 'commencing operations' with an 'innovative and repeatable business model with great global growth potential', and 'not older than 10 years'.
programmes.customer_access: None directly; a gateway to the Estonian ecosystem.
programmes.network_quality: Gateway to the Estonian ecosystem — Startup Wise Guys, Tehnopol and Buildit all sit downstream.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a signal, high as an enabler.
programmes.application_effort: Dealum form plus supporting documents, est. 6-10 hours. State fee €80 for a long-stay D visa, €60 for short-stay; no fee for the Startup Committee review itself.
programmes.notes: The stated criterion is 'an MVP and the first traction'. Supaprod has the MVP and no traction, so the second half is a real argument to win, not a formality. Still the cheapest and fastest EU entity-plus-residency combination in this lane, and it does not trip the India/FEMA problem an Indian entity would. It is also the unlock for the Tehnopol AI Accelerator, which requires an Estonian-registered company.

programmes.name: Lithuania Startup Visa
programmes.page_evidence: The dedicated programme site startupvisalithuania.com loads and invites applications with no deadline and no closure notice, and serves the Dealum apply link above. programmes.cash: None.
programmes.credits_and_tools: None. 'Startup Lithuania does not charge or ask for any kind of compensation from its applicants for their services.'

programmes.location_requirement: Lithuania. Incorporation comes AFTER the permit, which is the key structural detail: 'After receiving your TRP, you must officially establish your business in 120 days.'
programmes.customer_access: Startup Lithuania connects founders to mentors, investors and incubators.
programmes.network_quality: Vilnius fintech/AI cluster; Startup Lithuania is the national ecosystem coordinator.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a signal, moderate as an enabler.

programmes.notes: CORRECTION to phase 1: the apply URL is a different Dealum form (application/new/98601/...) from the one phase 1 carried, and the authoritative site is startupvisalithuania.com, not the startuplithuania.com landing page, which only links onward. The 120-days-after-TRP incorporation rule is the attractive part: no entity exists at any point in the application, and the founder controls when the Lithuanian UAB comes into being. Cheaper and faster than the Danish route.

programmes.name: Residence permit for foreign startups (Startup Visa, facilitator route)

programmes.cohort_dates: One-year permit; rolling application via IND with RVO assessing the plan.
programmes.cash: None from the state.
programmes.credits_and_tools: None from the state; the facilitator provides the support package.
programmes.terms_dilution: None from the state; facilitator terms vary.

programmes.network_quality: Depends entirely on the facilitator signed.

THREE of those are already on this list as programmes — Antler, Rockstart and HighTechXL — so an acceptance at any of them solves the visa and the programme in one move. Pursue as a consequence of an accelerator win, never as a standalone application.

programmes.name: Beyond Beta — Batch #15
programmes.page_evidence: The programme page invites applications now: 'Are you ready to scale Beyond Beta? The application round for Batch #15 opens on August 10, 2026. Apply here'. No closing date is published and there is no closure notice. CAVEAT ON THE FORM ITSELF: the apply URL returns HTTP 302 with a Location header pointing back to the same path — a redirect loop for any client without an established session — so I could not reach the form. It is the only apply link on the site.

programmes.credits_and_tools: Two mentors per team throughout the programme, one industry expert and one startup expert, with 'no financial stake in your business'. Networking at TechBBQ.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Published criterion: 'Have a committed founder team.' No minimum number given.
programmes.location_requirement: Denmark, via the CVR requirement.
programmes.customer_access: Danish industry clusters and investor network.
programmes.network_quality: Medium-high in Denmark; '60% of Beyond Beta alumni have raised funding'.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 4-8 hours once the form is reachable.

The criterion is explicit about timing: 'The CVR-number of the company may not be older than 7 years, when you submit your application.' programmes.notes: Free, EU-funded and open right now, but sequenced behind Startup Denmark plus Danish incorporation, which puts it out of reach this year. The other published criteria are met or nearly met: 'Onboarded your first users or customers, or at least an MVP that can be launched within the duration of the program' — the 'or at least an MVP' clause means zero users is explicitly acceptable here, which is unusual and worth remembering.

programmes.name: Accelerator Program (Accelerate)
